inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E owner FCF of ~$400m against FY2025's $467.7m. H1-2026 FCF collapsed 38% to $179.1m (OCF 369.0 down 10.1%, capex 189.9 up 57.8%). Note SFM reports in THOUSANDS and FY2026 is a 53-week year, so H1 cannot be doubled to annualise.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blend of equity 5yr CAGR (9.7%) and revenue 5yr CAGR (7.6%), decelerating
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR (30.5%) is far above revenue CAGR, driven by margin expansion (gross margin 36.9%->38.8%, operating margin 5.1%->7.8%) and aggressive buybacks (shares 103.4M FY2023 -> 94.6M Q1-2026). These tailwinds are largely realized; base case decelerates growth toward unit-growth + low-single-digit comps and assumes margins hold rather than keep expanding. The Q1-2026 comp turning NEGATIVE (-1.7%) confirms the deceleration is underway.

base.rationale: Base case assumes ~8% unit growth (40+ new stores/yr off a 477-store base) plus low-single-digit comps, decelerating as the exceptional 2024-25 comp surge normalizes (Q1-2026 comp already -1.7%). FCF margin held at FY2025 actual ~5.3% (467.7M / 8806.2M). WACC 8.5% reflects a debt-free balance sheet with net cash, beta ~1.0-1.2, risk-free ~4.3%. Terminal growth 2.5% (mature staples retailer, below GDP).

bull.rationale: Bull case assumes comps re-accelerate after the 2026 air-pocket, loyalty program drives customer data and traffic, self-distribution expands margin, and unit growth accelerates with strong new-store returns. Health/wellness secular tailwind continues; Sprouts keeps taking share from conventional grocers.

bear.rationale: Bear case: the negative Q1-2026 comp marks the start of sustained comp weakness as the 2024-25 new-customer surge fully unwinds, recession drives trade-down to Walmart/Aldi/Costco, competition compresses margins, and California concentration (33% of stores) creates regional risk. FCF margin compresses to 4.5% and base-year FCF haircut 15%.

sensitivity.notes: Sensitivity matrix shows base-case intrinsic value per share across WACC and terminal growth. At the current price of $81.85, the market is implying roughly the bottom-right region (WACC ~10% and/or terminal growth ~1.5-2%), i.e. it is pricing in continued comp weakness. Most central assumptions (WACC 8.5%, TG 2.5%) produce IV ~$106, ~29% above current.

probability_weighted.rationale: Base 50% (most likely: unit-growth-led, normalizing comps). Bull 25% and bear 25% balanced given the fresh negative Q1-2026 comp adds genuine two-sided uncertainty. Weighted IV ~$103 vs price $81.85 implies ~25% upside on a probability-weighted basis.

valuation_commentary.current_valuation: At $81.85 the stock has roughly halved from its ~$165 peak (Jan 2026) even as FY2025 fundamentals improved (revenue +14% to $8.8B, EPS $5.31, FCF ~$468M). The de-rating was driven by comp-sales normalization that turned negative (-1.7%) in Q1-2026. The stock now trades around 15x trailing EPS and ~9x EV/EBITDA, near the middle of its 10-year range.
valuation_commentary.key_drivers: Valuation hinges on whether the negative Q1-2026 comp is a temporary air-pocket against extreme prior-year comparisons (+11.7% Q1-2025) or the start of sustained weakness. Unit growth (~8-10%/yr) and FCF margin (~5.3%) are the durable drivers; comp trajectory and margin durability are the swing factors.
valuation_commentary.risks_to_valuation: Sustained negative comps, recession-driven trade-down, margin compression from competition (Walmart, Costco, Whole Foods, Aldi), California concentration (33% of stores), and execution risk on loyalty/self-distribution. Bear case IV $59 implies ~27% further downside.
valuation_commentary.upside_to_valuation: Comps re-accelerating, loyalty program monetization, self-distribution margin gains, and continued buybacks (shares already down from 99.3M to 94.6M) compounding per-share value. Bull case IV $140 implies ~71% upside.
valuation_commentary.recommendation: After the ~50% drawdown, the risk/reward has flipped from clearly overvalued (Jan 2026) to roughly fair-to-attractive. Base IV ~$106 (29% upside) and probability-weighted IV ~$103 (25% upside). The 15%-CAGR entry price is ~$60 (27% below current), so disciplined value buyers may want a further pullback, but the stock is no longer pricing in heroic assumptions.

q1_2026_actual.notes: Comparable store sales turned negative (-1.7%) vs +11.7% in Q1-2025 — the key de-rating catalyst. Revenue still grew on new-store unit growth (483 stores).

sanity_check.diagnosis: Base-case IV $105.57 implies P/E 19.9x (below 10yr avg 21.4x), P/B 7.12x (below 10yr max 9.55x), EV/EBITDA 11.5x (below 10yr max 19.6x). Base-year FCF $467.7M is the FY2025 actual, not an extrapolated peak, and FCF 3yr CAGR (15.9%) is reasonable for a grower opening 40+ stores/yr. Base-case upside is only 29% (<100%) and the price sits in the middle of the 10yr range. No sanity trip.
sanity_check.fix_applied: None required — all implied multiples sit within the company's own 10-year trading history.

sanity_check_verdict.reason: Weighted IV $78.5 vs price $81.04 (-3.1%), rebuilt on Q2-2026 actuals.
sanity_check_verdict.value_investor_conclusion: Roughly fairly valued at -3%. A quality grocer whose comps have turned negative while capex accelerates; there is no margin of safety here until either comps stabilise or the price does the work.

fields_updated: full model rebuild on Q2-2026 actuals

valuation_philosophy: Rebuilt 2026-08-28 on Q2-2026. The growth engine has reversed: comparable store sales went from +10.2% to -1.0% year-on-year, an 11-point swing. Total sales still grew 4.7% but entirely from new stores; operating income FELL 2.9% in Q2 and 4.0% in H1, and net income fell $4.5m. Meanwhile capex is up 57.8% and D&A up 17.7%, so the company is spending harder into decelerating comps -- OCF down 10% while capex is up 58% took H1 FCF from $290.0m to $179.1m. The prior 9%/8%/7% growth path assumed the comp engine still ran. Base now assumes new-store growth only. The balance sheet remains genuinely clean (no drawn credit facility; only finance obligations and leases), which is why the bear is a de-rating rather than distress. Management bought back stock at an average $80.93 this quarter against $158.99 a year ago -- a 49% decline in their own entry price, which is context, not endorsement.
